summary: Tenant burst traffic caused cascading 502s at API proxy and unhealthy upstreams leading to runtime restarts
description: AtlasRetail reported a sudden increase in 502 errors for their production routes after a traffic surge. Errors are observed at the API proxy layer with upstreams marked unhealthy and several serving runtime worker processes restarting under load. Customer reports higher latency and partial request failures across their pinned model routes.
impact: ~15% of requests for AtlasRetail returned 502 during the peak (12:10-12:35 UTC). Multiple realtime features degraded (recommendations and chat) for their enterprise customers. No broad customer-facing status page incident was triggered, but SLA exposure for this tenant is possible if unresolved.
steps_to_reproduce: Scale a single tenant's traffic from 50 RPS to 1200 RPS within 1 minute against pinned model route
Observe API gateway returning 502 and upstream health checks flipping to UNHEALTHY
Confirm serving-runtime worker processes restart logs and OOM/killed-by-kernel not present
logs: 2026-03-13T12:12:07Z apigw[proxy-12] ERROR upstream response 502 for tenant=atlas_tenant route=/v1/generate
2026-03-13T12:12:09Z runtime[worker-7] WARN eviction: kv-cache thrash detected (cache miss ratio 86%)
2026-03-13T12:12:18Z autoscaler INFO scale_down suppressed due to recent restarts for pool=dedicated-us-east-atlas
investigation_notes: Initial metrics show a sharp request concurrency spike for AtlasRetail routes starting 12:09 UTC
API gateway connection pool saturating: #active connections reached configured proxy limit and started returning 502 to client
Upstream health checks started failing 502/503 and api-gateway marked multiple serving-runtime instances as UNHEALTHY which triggered retries and increased load on remaining instances
Serving runtime logs show continuous eviction and GC spikes; not classical OOMs but process restarts correlated with high load and frequent cache thrashing
comments: Ava Chen (Support): Customer reported customer-visible failures at 12:15 UTC. Collected request IDs and sample payloads.
Diego Morales (SRE): Looking at proxy metrics and connection limits; temporarily increasing connection pool and enabling short-term burst window for atlas-account to mitigate.
Lina Patel (Customer Success): Notified AtlasRetail with temporary mitigation steps and requested peak traffic schedule for permanent solution.
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporary increase of api-gateway upstream_conn_limit for AtlasRetail and enabled aggressive KV cache TTL to reduce thrash. Result: 502 rate fell below 1% within 10 minutes. Root cause hypothesized as concentrated short-lived burst exceeding per-tenant connection and cache capacity; long-term fix required.
next_steps: Engineering to validate autoscaler burst policy for dedicated pools (assigned to INT-4118)
Platform to add per-tenant burst windows and graceful shedding before marking upstream UNHEALTHY
Follow-up with AtlasRetail on traffic shaping and recommended client backoff settings
Create dashboard alert for sudden per-tenant RPS growth + proxy connection saturation
